text:
jordan_m: Heads-up — starting phased enablement for structured-output / function-calling support next week. Need to align on flag names, client SDK behavior, and minimal guardrails. Quick Qs: who owns the client-side compat changes? and what should default fallback be if a client doesn't opt in?

sophia: I can take ownership of SDK changes (JS + Python) but will need clear contract — exact flag semantics and runtime fallback.

samir: From runtime side: we should expose two flags — one for server-side compatibility mode (so_compat_mode) and one for client opt-in (so_client_opt_in). Server flag controls payload shape returned to callers.

lucy: Also want to ensure evals team has a testset for regressions. If we flip structured output on for some customers, we need canary coverage and quality monitors.

jordan_m: proposed flag names:
```
SO_CLIENT_OPT_IN = "so_client_opt_in_v1"  # client-side opt-in toggle
SO_COMPAT_MODE = "so_compat_v1"        # server returns compat payloads when on
```
If SO_COMPAT_MODE = off, runtime will try to return structured output natively. If client not opted-in, route to compat shim.

oliver: +1 on two-flag approach. Couple of guardrails:
- default: compat mode ON for existing customers
- canary audience: internal + 5 customers with heavy test suites
- metric hooks: so.success_rate, so.format_errors, so.latency_p50/p95
Can we add audit log entries when shim is used?

sophia: yep — SDK will emit a telemetry event when receiving compat-shim payloads. Will need the exact event fields.

samir: runtime will add a header `x-so-variant: shim|native` and emit a metric tag `so_variant` for tracing. That should make dashboards + alerts straightforward.

jordan_m: plan for rollout timeline:
- Mon: create feature flags + gating in LaunchDarkly (ops will create namespaces)
- Tue-Wed: SDK PRs for opt-in and telemetry (sophia)
- Wed: runtime change behind SO_COMPAT_MODE default=true (samir)
- Thu: internal canary (eng + qa)
- Week after: 5 external canaries, monitor metrics for 72h

sophia: SDK behavior question — if a client sets so_client_opt_in_v1=true but server is still in compat mode (so_compat_v1=true), should SDK still request native? or respect server final shape?

samir: SDK should always be prepared for compat payloads. If client opt-in but server still compat, server will return compat-shaped response; SDK should map compat -> structured-friendly objects and emit telemetry that shim mapping occurred.

lucy: add a regression alert: if so.format_errors increases by >3x baseline in 24h, auto-disable external canary and notify #incidents.

oliver: good. add a circuit-breaker config in runtime: error-rate threshold and automatic rollback to compat for that customer id. Also capture a sample of raw responses for debugging (sanitized).

jordan_m: noted — samir can you add a rollout flag that supports per-customer override? and a way to pin model variant?

samir: yes — will add per-customer override and model-pin via config. Example request header we accept: `x-customer-overrides: {"so_mode":"native","model":"redwood-v2"}` (we'll accept only signed override tokens in prod).

sophia: I'm going to open the SDK PRs later today. I'll include a small migration doc and examples:
- how to opt-in
- how to detect shim vs native (`response.meta.so_variant`)
- telemetry event schema

jordan_m: FYI deploy-bot will post canary deploy notes.

deploy-bot: [deploy] staging/runtime:so-compat-toggle @jordan_m samir scheduled at 2024-08-12T03:00:00Z :rocket:

oliver: last ask — please add an internal tracking ticket for the canary customers + rollback owners. Make sure support has playbook and canned messages.

jordan_m: will create GH issue and ping @support. Thanks everyone — we'll reconvene Fri for a quick post-canary sync. :thumbsup:
